issues.legal_issue: State ownership of mineral deposits on government land is not displaced by legislation regulating mines and mineral development.
material_facts: The mineral deposits at issue were located on land owned by the State.
The dispute concerned applications for mining leases, and the applicants did not seriously dispute the State’s ownership of the minerals.
issues.conclusion: The State owns mineral deposits in government-owned land within its territory, while the applicable legislation regulates their development without divesting that ownership.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2 of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, read with Entry 54 of List I and Entry 23 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, places regulation and development of mines and minerals under Union control to the extent provided by the Act; it does not transfer State ownership of minerals. The Court relied on Monnet Ispat and Energy Limited v. Union of India and Amritlal Nathubhai Shah v. Union of India.

predicates.mining_lease_dispute: The proceeding concerns a dispute over the grant or refusal of a mining lease.
predicates.mineral_deposits_on_government_owned_lan: The mineral deposits are located on land owned by the State.

issues.definition: When a mining-lease dispute concerns minerals on State-owned land, State ownership remains while being subject to mining regulation.

issues.legal_issue: A State industrial policy reserving mineral exploitation to public-sector entities does not constitute a valid statutory reservation or justify refusing mining-lease applications unless the statutory reservation requirements are met.
material_facts: The State adopted an industrial policy under which mineral-sand mining would be undertaken only through public-sector undertakings.
The State had not obtained the Central Government’s approval for a reservation and had not issued an official-gazette notification specifying the reserved areas and minerals.
The lease applications concerned areas not already held under prospecting licences or mining leases.
The State rejected the applications by relying on its policy reserving exploitation to public-sector undertakings.
The High Court set aside the State’s rejection, and the State appealed.
issues.conclusion: The policy did not amount to a valid reservation under the Act, so the State could not rely on it as a reservation to refuse the applications; the State could make a valid reservation later by following the statutory procedure. The appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17A(2) of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, permits the State to reserve an area not already held under a prospecting licence or mining lease for mining through a government company or corporation, with Central Government approval and an official-gazette notification specifying the area’s boundaries and the minerals. A statutory act must be done in the prescribed manner; a general executive policy cannot replace that procedure. The Court relied on Commissioner of Income Tax v. Anjum M.H. Ghaswala, Captain Sube Singh v. Lt. Governor of Delhi, State of U.P. v. Singhara Singh, Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner, Sandur Manganese and Iron Ores Ltd. v. State of Karnataka, and Bharat Coking Coal Ltd. v. State of Bihar.

rule.if: supreme_court_appeal_over_mining_lease_refusal and state_policy_reserves_mining_to_public_entities and not (central_approval_obtained and area_not_already_licensed_or_leased and official_notification_specifies_area_and_mineral)

predicates.supreme_court_appeal_over_mining_lease_r: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the refusal of applications for mining leases.
predicates.state_policy_reserves_mining_to_public_e: The State adopted a policy limiting the relevant mining activity to public-sector entities.
predicates.central_approval_obtained: The State obtained the Central Government’s approval for the reservation.
predicates.area_not_already_licensed_or_leased: The area proposed for reservation was not already held under a prospecting licence or mining lease.
predicates.official_notification_specifies_area_and: The State published an official notification specifying the boundaries of the reserved area and the mineral or minerals covered.

issues.definition: If a State relies on a policy reserving mining to public-sector entities to refuse a lease application, but one or more statutory reservation requirements is absent, the policy is not a valid reservation and cannot support that refusal.
